answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, a pure switch to the low-cost vendor could meet the 18% mandate on price but raises delivery/transition risk; deferral is unsafe because the primary contract lapses. The intended single move is to renegotiate with the incumbent before expiry using the low-cost quote as a market benchmark and, if needed, a longer/multi-year commitment to unlock volume pricing while preserving service scope and continuity. I want to verify the renewal-benchmarking result and the multi-year incumbent pricing result before relying on them to hit as much of the mandate as possible without adding delivery risk.
